title: A query built from input
context: The search term comes from a request. Select the unsafe line.
code: var sql = "SELECT Id, Name FROM Items WHERE Name = '" + term + "'";
using var command = new SqlCommand(sql, connection);
explanation: The input is concatenated into SQL syntax. An input containing quote characters can change the query's meaning.
fix: Use a parameterised query, for example WHERE Name = @name, then add the term as a parameter.
test: Use a quote and SQL-looking input, then verify it is treated as a literal search value.

title: A record ID is not permission
context: The route receives an item ID from the caller.
explanation: The code loads a record without checking whether the current user may access it. Knowing an identifier must not grant access.
fix: Apply a server-side ownership or policy check before returning the record.
test: Sign in as one user and request a record belonging to another user. Expect a denial.

title: A state change accepts ambient credentials
context: A cookie-authenticated endpoint changes an account preference.
explanation: If cookie authentication is used, a cross-site request may cause a state change unless the application's CSRF protections are applied.
fix: Use the framework's appropriate anti-forgery protection and validate request origin where suitable.
test: Submit a cross-origin state-changing request and confirm the server rejects it.

title: A user-controlled URL is fetched
context: A preview endpoint accepts a URL to retrieve.
explanation: A caller can ask the server to make requests to destinations the caller cannot reach directly, including internal addresses.
fix: Prefer an allowlist of permitted hosts and schemes, block private and link-local ranges, and validate redirects and resolved addresses.
test: Try loopback, private-network, metadata-like and redirecting URLs in a controlled test environment.

title: Spreadsheet cells are not always plain text
context: The export includes a value supplied by a user.
explanation: CSV quoting handles delimiters and quotes, but a cell beginning with formula characters can still be interpreted by spreadsheet software.
fix: Apply a documented spreadsheet-safe policy to dangerous leading characters, then quote and escape the cell. Test the target spreadsheet applications.
test: Export values beginning with equals, plus, minus and at-sign, then inspect how they open in a spreadsheet.

title: A fast hash is not password storage
context: The app stores a digest for later login checks.
explanation: A fast general-purpose hash makes large-scale password guessing cheaper, and this example has no per-password salt or work factor.
fix: Use the platform's password-hashing implementation with a unique salt and a suitable work factor. Do not design a password hash format yourself.
test: Review the stored format and verify that the framework's password verification API is used.

title: A key committed with the source
context: This constant is used to sign application tokens.
explanation: A secret in source can be copied into repository history and every clone. Renaming the variable does not protect the value.
fix: Load secrets from an appropriate runtime secret store or injected environment configuration, and rotate any exposed key.
test: Scan repository history and verify the application fails safely when required secret configuration is absent.

title: A parse result is ignored
context: The field should contain a whole number.
explanation: Converting input does not prove it is a finite integer or within the business range. Values such as empty strings or decimals may be accepted unexpectedly.
fix: Validate type, finiteness, integer status and the documented minimum and maximum before saving.
test: Try empty, whitespace, decimal, negative, huge and non-numeric values.

title: Redirect target comes from the query
context: After sign-in, the app redirects to a return URL.
explanation: A caller can supply a destination outside the application, which can make a trusted sign-in flow useful for phishing.
fix: Accept only local relative paths or compare the destination against a strict allowlist of trusted origins.
test: Try an absolute external URL, a protocol-relative URL and a valid local path.

title: An internal exception is returned
context: A route catches an exception while processing a request.
explanation: Exception messages can contain internal paths, query details or implementation information. Returning them leaks details to callers.
fix: Return a generic error with a correlation identifier, and keep appropriate diagnostic details in access-controlled logs.
test: Force an exception and confirm the response has no stack, secret or internal path.

title: A filename is joined without confinement
context: A download endpoint accepts a filename.
explanation: Path combination alone does not confine a caller-supplied path to the intended directory. Traversal segments can escape the root.
fix: Resolve the full path, verify it remains under the intended root using a correct path comparison, and prefer opaque IDs mapped to known files.
test: Try parent-directory segments, encoded separators and absolute paths on the target operating system.

title: Untrusted text becomes HTML
context: A search term is displayed in a result panel.
explanation: The browser parses the user-controlled string as HTML, so markup can become executable content.
fix: Use textContent for plain text, or apply a reviewed sanitisation approach when rich HTML is genuinely required.
test: Enter a harmless markup string and verify it is displayed as text, not parsed into elements.
